c.tagline: Riverside chaos, Mughal history, and relentless energy on the Buriganga.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but many drivers prefer flat/negotiated fares; CNG auto-rickshaws technically metered but usually negotiated; rideshare apps (Pathao, Uber) give upfront pricing and are the most reliable option.

emergency.medical: 999 or 199 (ambulance); Tourist Police available in key areas
emergency.note: 999 is the free 24/7 national emergency hotline covering police, fire, and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Petty crime and gridlock; caution at political demonstrations/hartals (can turn violent); pickpocketing in crowds

hood_desc: Upscale diplomatic and business enclave with international restaurants, embassies and Dhaka's best hotels; suits business travelers and those wanting comfort and easy airport access.
Trendy residential-commercial area next to Gulshan with rooftop cafes, boutiques and nightlife-adjacent dining; good for mid-range travelers wanting a lively, walkable base.
Leafy, laid-back academic and cultural neighborhood around Dhanmondi Lake with cafes, bookshops and Bengali cultural sites; suits budget-to-mid travelers and those wanting local flavor.
Chaotic, historic riverside old quarter with Mughal-era monuments, Sadarghat river port and street food; suits adventurous travelers prioritizing heritage and atmosphere over comfort.
Central business and diplomatic district near Sonargaon roundabout with large hotels and convention facilities; suits conference-goers and travelers wanting a central, well-connected base.

water.note: Tap water is unsafe due to aging pipes, contamination, and arsenic concerns; use bottled or filtered water.

transit.pay: Metro uses rechargeable MRT/Rapid Pass cards or single-journey tokens from station kiosks/machines. Buses are pay-by-cash to a conductor on board. Ferries and rickshaws are cash-only, fares often negotiated.
transit.hours: Metro roughly 7:10am-9:20pm; buses run early morning to around 10-11pm; limited late-night options rely on rideshare apps or negotiated CNGs.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is severe; the Metro (opened 2022, still expanding) is the fastest way to cross the city during peak hours.

ferry: Sadarghat river terminal launches to southern Bangladesh

airport.name: Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (DAC)
airport.drive: 30-50 min depending on traffic (can exceed 1hr in rush hour)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or 5-10% appreciated at upscale restaurants and hotels; not expected for taxis/rickshaws though small change is welcomed.

food.name: Kacchi biryani
food.desc: Raw marinated mutton layered with ghee-rich rice, potato and kewra, sealed and slow-cooked; Dhaka's wedding dish and its greatest argument.

places.name: Haji Biryani
places.note: Decades-old Old Dhaka name; small, no-frills and always crowded.

places.name: Nanna Biryani
places.note: Traditional Old Dhaka kacchi cooked with heavy ghee and whole spice.

places.name: Sultan's Dine
places.note: Modern chain most often named for consistent kacchi if you want comfort and air conditioning.

food.name: Bhuna khichuri
food.desc: Rice and lentils fried with whole spice until every grain separates, served with beef bhuna, egg and pickle, especially on rainy days.

places.name: Star Kabab & Restaurant
places.note: Dhaka institution with branches citywide, reliable for khichuri and beef.

places.name: Hotel Al Razzaque
places.note: Long-established Old Dhaka kitchen known for khichuri, kebab and mutton dishes.

places.name: Nirab Hotel
places.note: Cheap, famously busy local hotel serving khichuri and bhuna all day.

food.name: Shorshe ilish
food.desc: Hilsa, the national fish, steamed or simmered in a pungent mustard-and-green-chilli paste and eaten with plain rice, bones and all.

places.name: Kasturi Restaurant
places.note: Long-running Bengali kitchen known for hilsa and other river fish.

places.name: Hotel Al Razzaque
places.note: Traditional preparation of ilish alongside the beef and mutton curries.

places.name: Ghoroa Restaurant
places.note: Home-style Bengali chain that keeps mustard hilsa on the menu in season.

food.name: Fuchka and chotpoti
food.desc: Crisp hollow shells stuffed with spiced potato and chickpea, doused in tamarind water; chotpoti is the soupier bowl version with boiled egg.

places.name: Rabindra Sarobar, Dhanmondi Lake
places.note: Lakeside carts are the most popular evening fuchka spot in the new city.

places.name: TSC and Dhaka University area
places.note: Student-priced fuchka and chotpoti carts running until late.

places.name: Chawkbazar
places.note: Historic market street thick with street-food stalls, especially in Ramadan.

food.name: Shik kebab and beef bhuna
food.desc: Minced or cubed beef and mutton grilled on skewers over coals, eaten with paratha or naan; Old Dhaka's evening staple.

places.name: Bismillah Kabab & Biryani
places.note: Known for both kebabs and a strongly spiced kacchi.

places.name: Star Kabab & Restaurant
places.note: The name says it; grilled meats and parathas at all hours.

places.name: Hotel Al Razzaque
places.note: Charcoal kebabs served with the restaurant's own naan.

food.name: Mishti doi
food.desc: Sweet yoghurt set in clay pots with caramelised sugar, thick enough to cut; the standard end to any Bengali meal.

places.name: Premium Sweets
places.note: Widely available sweet shop chain with dependable clay-pot mishti doi.

places.name: Banaphool
places.note: Bangladeshi sweet house selling doi alongside roshogolla and shondesh.

places.name: Muslim Sweets
places.note: Old-city mishtanno bhandar for traditional sweets bought by the pot.

food.name: Borhani
food.desc: Cold savoury yoghurt drink cut with mustard, mint, black salt and green chilli; the traditional partner to kacchi biryani.

places.name: Sultan's Dine
places.note: Served by the glass with every kacchi platter.

places.name: Haji Biryani
places.note: Old Dhaka biryani houses pour borhani to cut the ghee.

places.name: Star Kabab & Restaurant
places.note: Easy place to try borhani with grilled meat rather than biryani.

food.name: Lassi and cha
food.desc: Thick sweet or salted yoghurt lassi by day, and endless small cups of milky, sugary cha from roadside tong stalls at every other hour.

places.name: Beauty Lassi
places.note: Old Dhaka landmark that has been pouring lassi and faluda for generations.

places.name: Chawkbazar
places.note: Lassi and sherbet vendors line the market lanes, busiest before iftar.

places.name: Dhanmondi tong stalls
places.note: Roadside tea stands doing malai cha and masala cha into the night.

landmarks: Ahsan Manzil (Pink Palace)
This rosy pink former palace of the Nawab of Dhaka on the Buriganga River is one of the city's most photogenic 19th-century landmarks.
Lalbagh Fort
An unfinished 17th-century Mughal fort complex with mosques, a tomb, and gardens that offers a glimpse into Dhaka's Mughal heritage.
National Parliament House (Jatiyo Sangsad Bhaban)
Louis Kahn's monumental modernist masterpiece is one of the largest legislative complexes in the world and a striking architectural icon.
Star Mosque (Tara Masjid)
A small but dazzling mosque covered in intricate blue-and-white star mosaic tilework, beloved by photographers.
National Martyrs' Memorial (Jatiyo Smriti Soudho)
A striking series of concrete triangular spires just outside Dhaka commemorating those who died in the 1971 Liberation War.
Dhakeshwari Temple
The 'Temple of the City Goddess' and Bangladesh's most important Hindu temple, known for its colorful architecture and vibrant festivals.
Baitul Mukarram National Mosque
Bangladesh's national mosque, an imposing cube-shaped structure inspired by the Kaaba and a major spiritual and civic landmark.
Buriganga River & Sadarghat Boat Terminal
One of the world's busiest river terminals, offering an unforgettable, chaotic, colorful scene of wooden boats and river life.
Curzon Hall
A striking blend of Mughal and European architecture built in 1904, now part of Dhaka University's picturesque campus.
Liberation War Museum
A moving museum documenting Bangladesh's 1971 independence struggle, essential for understanding the nation's identity.

train.note: Domestic trains leave from Kamalapur (Dhaka) station. The cross-border trains to India - Maitree Express (Kolkata) and Mitali Express (New Jalpaiguri) - have been suspended since August 2024 and remained halted through mid-2026, so do not count on them without checking first.

bus.note: Cross-border coaches to India run despite the train suspension, but service can be disrupted by India-Bangladesh political tensions - confirm before travel. Carry your passport and Indian visa; you change buses at the Benapole/Petrapole border.

ferry.note: No international passenger ferries operate from Dhaka. The city's famous domestic river launches depart from Sadarghat terminal for southern destinations like Barisal.
